name: Revenge for Dino
description: A physics combat game on a gamified Google search page, where Gemini generates playable objects from natural language in real time.

sections.alt: The Crash boss looms on a Google search page while Gemini displays generated Planck.js code in a speech bubble
The Crash boss corrupts the Google search page while the dinosaur ragdoll braces for impact

text: Team up with Gemini to defeat the Collapsing Corrupting Core of Crashes.

Type anything into the search bar and watch Gemini build it in real time, code and all, and drop it into the game. Each object is one-shot generated: body, physics, behavior, and logic, injected live into a Box2D simulation.

The game disguises itself as a Google search page. Every element on the page, the logo, the buttons, the navigation links, are real physics bodies. Players type natural language prompts into the search bar, and Gemini generates executable Planck.js code in real time, spawning autonomous objects that can be dragged, thrown, and hurled at a growing void enemy.

The boss is a corrupting core that devours everything it touches. Its one vulnerability is a roaming eye on its perimeter. Hit it hard enough, and it takes damage. Let it grow too large, and the game is over.

sections.alt: A toy train with smoke particles rolls along the ground, generated from a search prompt
An olive-green tank with a crosshair targets the enemy
A rain cloud drops blue particles that accumulate on the ground

text: A two-model pipeline powers object creation. Gemini 2.0 Flash normalizes prompts into cache keys, while Gemini 3 Pro writes the actual Planck.js code. Generated functions are sandboxed and executed live, creating bodies, joints, and update loops that interact with the existing physics world.
A two-tier caching system (curated objects locally, novel generations in Firebase) means popular objects load instantly, while new prompts trigger fresh generation.

sections.alt: Side-by-side comparison of Gemini 2 Flash and Gemini 3 Pro generating objects from the same prompt
The full game interface mimicking a Google search page in a browser, with the Crash boss lurking in the corner

text: The entire Google search page is recreated in Canvas. Every UI element, from logo letters to footer links, exists as a Box2D static body. Drag any element and it converts to a dynamic body, subject to gravity and the void's gravitational pull. The Gemini companion, an animated star icon, follows your cursor, flies to the spawn location, and delivers each new creation.

With AI dominating conversations everywhere, it is crucial to give people hands-on experience with the model and to differentiate in the market. This project shows rather than tells. It takes something uniquely Google, the search page, and something uniquely Gemini, real-time code generation, and turns them into a playable experience.
